contexts.text: A staff of reed () = such power.
To break the staff of bread () = to be deprived of heavenly food.
Their staff will indicate it () = the imaginary power of their own understanding.
The staff of bread, and the staff of water, which shall be removed, () = the good and the truth.
Their staves () = the power which they have.
Levi's rod blossomed (). Explained.

Jacob took a fresh rod of poplar () = the power proper to natural good. A rod, when mentioned in the Word, always = power, both from the fact that shepherds use it for exercising power over their flocks, and because it serves for the support of the body, and as it were for the right hand. Therefore a rod was used by kings, and the royal badge was a short staff, and also a sceptre. It was also used by priests and prophets, that they also by their rod might signify the power which they had, as Aaron and Moses, and therefore Moses was so frequently commanded to stretch out his rod... From the signification of a rod as power, the Egyptian magi made use of it when they performed their magical miracles...

But, in the Original, the rods used by shepherds, kings, priests, and prophets, are expressed by another word; here, by a word by which is expressed the staff of travellers, and also that of shepherds. Illustrated. Here, indeed, the rod is not mentioned as supporting the hand, but as a rod cut from a tree... but still it has the same signification.
The rods = power. AC 4016. AC 4019. AC 4030.
A staff () = power, and is predicated of truth.
A staff = the power of truth from good.
The staff which is in thy hand () = by the power of that truth.

The reason a staff (or rod) = power, is that it is a support, for it supports the hand and arm, and thereby the whole body, and therefore a staff puts on the signification of that part which it proximately supports, namely, that of the hand and arm.
That by a rod was represented power. Illustrated.
The hand is the principal, and the rod the instrumental. Illustrated.
From these passages it is evident that a rod, like the hand, represented power; and, in the supreme sense, the Divine omnipotence of the Lord.
That a staff (or rod) = power. Further illustrated.
Thy rod, and Thy staff () = the Divine truth and good, in which is power.
The power was not in Moses' rod, but solely in the Divine command.

Spirits have appeared who had rods: they were magicians... They seem to themselves to have rods, and by phantasies they form many kinds of rods, and believe that by them they can do miracles; for they suppose that there is force in the rods...
A rod () = power.
A long roll fastened to rods, seen.
What is that in thine hand? He said, A rod () = the power of the Lord's Divine Human. Explained.

The power signified by the hand, is the power proceeding from the Lord's Divine Rational; but that signified by the rod, is the power proceeding from His Divine Natural; because a rod (or staff) supports the body like a foot...
A rod = power in the Natural, and, when said of the Lord, the power proceeding from His Divine Natural. Explained. AC 6954.

Take this rod in thine hand () = the Divine power in them. A rod = power, when it is in the hand; for the hand = spiritual power, and a rod natural power. As there is no power in the Natural except from the Spiritual, so there is none in a rod unless it is in the hand... AC 7026.
Moses took the rod of God in his hand () = that those things were from Divine power... The rod of God = Divine power. AC 8599.

That a rod = power, derives its origin from the representatives (there); for those who exercise things magical appear with rods, which also are of service to them for powers; and hence the Egyptian magicians had rods, by which they did such things as appeared like miracles; and hence the Ancients in their writings everywhere assign rods to magicians. (Thus) a rod is a representative of power; and it is also a real correspondence, for power is actually exercised by means of rods; but this, with magicians, is an abuse of the correspondence, and does not avail except within the Hells where they are... And, as there is a real correspondence of a rod with power, Moses was commanded to take a rod in his hand, and by means of it do signs; and therefore, also, kings have a sceptre, which is a short rod, and by it is signified the royal power. The correspondence of a rod and of the power is from this, that a rod (or staff) supports the hand and arm, thus at the same time the body, and the hand and arm corresponds to power...
Take thy rod, and cast it before Pharaoh () = power which is shown. AC 7295. AC 7298.
(Such Spirits) form rods for themselves... and so exercise magical power.
Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods () = that power was taken away from them.
The rod which was turned into a serpent take in thine hand () = power like the former.
The rod = power.
The rod = natural power; the hand, spiritual power.
The rod = natural power, which is of external truth; and therefore the words, Stretch forth thine hand with thy rod = the power of internal truth through external truth.
Stretch forth thy rod = to exercise and show Divine power. Explained.
Moses stretched forth his rod towards heaven () = communication with Heaven. Explained.
Moses stretched out his rod over the land of Egypt () = the dominion of the power of truth Divine...
Your staff in your hand () = as to mediate things. Explained.
Take up thy rod () = the power of Divine truth.
Thy rod = Divine power.
Their staff answereth unto them () = the imaginary power from Man's Own Intellectual. AE 376:38.
That supporteth himself with a staff (), that is, one lame, = those with whom all good is destroyed.
The staff of bread = power from good; the staff of water = power from truth.
To smite... with a staff () = to ill-treat... from Own power. Explained.
The hand-staff () = the power of truth from good. ( = the power of truth; and, in the opposite, the power of falsity. AC 9228:2.)
The staff of bread = power and life from good; the staff of water = power and life from truth.
The staff of the foundation () = the power of truth.
A staff = the power of truth. References.
Holding in their hands shepherds' staves.
The dust in my garden, on being stirred with a stick, rose in clouds of insects.
A reed like unto a rod () = power from the Lord. Explained. (Compare AE 627.)
A rod = mighty power, which is from the Lord; here, that of Knowing the state of the Church, because the temple and altar were measured with the rod...

The reason power is signified by a rod, is that the wood of which the rods were made, among the Ancients = good; and because it is in place of the right hand, and supports it; and by the right hand is signified power. Hence it is that a sceptre is a short rod, and by a sceptre is signified the power of a king.
That a rod (or staff) = power. Illustrated.
A counterfeit wand (used by Sirens). SE 4598.
Those who use magic arts have rods.

The two words in the Hebrew for tribes = a sceptre and a rod, and by a sceptre is signified Divine truth as to government, and by a rod, Divine truth as to power. (Hence) it was commanded, when the people were murmuring... that the princes of all the tribes should place their rods in the tabernacle... and, in the midst of them, the rod of Levi, upon which was written the name of Aaron, and which yielded almonds (); for by rods the like is signified as by tribes, and by the rod of Levi (therefore) the good of charity... and the good of love. (Further explained.)

To remove all the staff of bread, and all the stay of water () = all the good of love and truth of faith... The staff, and the stay = powers, and thence all things of spiritual life. (Compare AE 727:12.)
The staff of Egypt shall depart away () = that scientifics inservient to reasonings will avail nought. AE 538:5. AE 654:24.
With their staves () = the power and forces of the mind; here, from the Lord through the Word.

The staff (of this bruised reed, Egypt) () = the power thence of perceiving, and also of reasoning about, truths... To lean upon this staff = to confide in one's own power of perceiving truths, and reasoning about them from the proprium.
Their confidence is signified by a staff of reed (). (Further explained.) AE 654:52.

That a rod, and a staff, = power, and indeed the power of Divine truth, is chiefly from the fact that they were boughs or branches of trees, and these = the Knowledges of truth and good, which are the truths of the natural man: and, as they also supported the body, they signified power; and, still more so an iron rod. Explained, Illustrated.

Thy rod, and Thy staff, shall comfort me = that Divine truth spiritual, together with Divine truth natural, will protect, because there is power in them. Rod = Divine truth spiritual; staff, Divine truth natural, both together as to the power of protecting.

How is the staff of strength broken, the rod of beauty () = that they no longer had Divine truth in its power. The staff of strength = this in the natural sense; and the rod of beauty = in the spiritual sense.
The rod of thy strength (Psalm Explained. 2) = Divine truth in its power.
As a staff = the power of Divine truth, it also = the power to resist evils and falsities. Illustrated.

As a rod, and a staff = the power of Divine truth, and thence Divine truth as to power, in the opposite sense, they = the power of infernal falsity, and thence infernal falsity as to power. Illustrated.
(In the Hells from the men of the Ancient Church) they go with rods in their hands. Explained.
